tools.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context. The workflow framework will treat this as a failure signal even when the agent exits successfully.

details.description: Optional extended details or diagnostic context about the failure (max 65000 characters).

reason.description: A concise explanation of why the task could not be completed (max 1024 characters). Be specific about which tools or resources were unavailable.

tools.name: report_incomplete

tools.description: Submit exactly one triage decision as separate fields for trusted validation.

comment.description: Public clarification text, or no_action (requires label no_action)

label.description: needs reproducible example, needs more info, or no_action (requires comment no_action)

rationale.description: Nonempty private justification for the decision

tools.name: submit_triage

arguments.comment: Could you provide the build-system files and pip/setuptools versions? Specifically, please attach the contents of `tools/pythonpkg/pyproject.toml` (or `setup.py` if present) and the output of `pip --version` and `python -c "import setuptools; print(setuptools.__version__)"`. These will show which build dependency provides `package_build` and whether the build environment installed it.
arguments.label: needs more info
arguments.rationale: The report shows a ModuleNotFoundError for `package_build` during pip's isolated build step. Reproducing this requires the package build-system declaration (pyproject.toml or setup.py) to know which build dependency should provide `package_build`, and the reporter's `pip`/`setuptools` versions to determine whether build dependencies are being installed into the isolated environment. Without these files and version details I cannot follow the exact failing setup.
